svg.title: Twenty loop shapes: a field guide to grooph's templates
svg.text: A field guide to grooph's templates for multi-agent work: what
each shape is, and when to reach for it.
Open any shape in the app:

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'Roboto Mono', monospace

g.title: Contradiction seeker: A claim can be broken by one concrete counterexample (a property, an invariant, an edge case), and a bounded search for it is worth more than an open-ended review.
g.text: A claim can be broken by one concrete
cost low · speed fast · rigor standard

g.title: Debate then build: Short adversarial planning, then a small build graph: the right approach is genuinely unclear and a wrong choice is expensive to undo.
g.text: Short adversarial planning, then a small build
cost medium · speed medium · rigor standard

g.title: Dual bar: The work needs both a ship line and a directional aspiration: good enough to ship is clear, and better is worth pointing at without ever blocking.
g.text: The work needs both a ship line and a
cost medium · speed medium · rigor standard

g.title: Fresh grind, rare judge: Cheap iteration most steps, an expensive critic at phase boundaries: long work splits into phases that tests can drive but only judgment can sign off.
g.text: Cheap iteration most steps, an expensive
cost medium · speed medium · rigor high

g.title: Gauntlet, decomposed: A rendered artifact must match a named reference and is too large for one owner and one critic: the pieces have real seams, each can be captured and judged alone, and they are coupled enough to build in sequence.
g.text: A rendered artifact must match a named
reference and is too large for one owner…
cost high · speed slow · rigor high

g.title: Grind loop: Done and good are the same: tests, types or a task list supply the back pressure, so a passing check is the finish line.
g.text: Done and good are the same: tests, types or
a task list supply the back pressure…
cost low · speed fast · rigor light

g.title: Heterogeneous critic: The judge should not share the builder's model when isolating taste or blind spots matters: a same-model critic keeps approving the mistakes the builder makes.
g.text: The judge should not share the builder's
model when isolating taste or blind spots…
cost medium · speed medium · rigor high

g.title: Metric sandwich: Cheap deterministic checks first, expensive judgment only on what those cannot see: lint and tests catch most failures, and a reviewer should not spend a round on them.
g.text: judgment only on what those cannot see…
cost medium · speed medium · rigor standard

g.title: Ownership, not swarm: Coupled subsystems get one owner; fan out only the independent pieces. The work spans a shared core and several leaf pieces that touch nothing else.
g.text: Coupled subsystems get one owner; fan out
cost medium · speed medium · rigor standard

g.title: Patrol pulse: Something should be looked at on a schedule (a log, a queue, a report) and the output of each look is a triaged record for a human, never a change: run the package under the harness's scheduler and each pulse is a run.
g.text: Something should be looked at on a schedule
cost low · speed fast · rigor standard

g.title: Ralph loop: The work is already a prioritised list of small items that tests can check one at a time, and you want a fresh context per item with the plan and an agent file as the only memory.
g.text: The work is already a prioritised list of small
items that tests can check one at a time…
cost low · speed fast · rigor light

g.title: Red-team loop: A separate attacker should produce failing traces and the builder should see only those: hardening against inputs or abuse nobody has listed yet.
g.text: A separate attacker should produce failing
traces and the builder should see…
cost medium · speed medium · rigor high

g.title: Retrospective rewrite: After a run, propose graph edits rather than rewriting mid-flight: the graph is being tuned across runs and the human wants every change as a proposal.
g.text: After a run, propose graph edits rather than
cost low · speed medium · rigor standard

g.title: Review gate: Work, then a separate reviewer, then iterate or pass: the change needs a second pair of eyes against a checklist that already exists.
g.text: Work, then a separate reviewer, then iterate
cost medium · speed medium · rigor standard

g.title: Spec then loop: No external reference product exists: a planning pass writes an answer key (ACCEPTANCE.md) that becomes the bar. The default for zero-to-one work.
g.text: No external reference product exists: a
planning pass writes an answer key…
cost medium · speed medium · rigor high

g.title: Specialist critic bank: Multiple disjoint judges (correctness, security, performance, taste) should each look at the change, and their findings need merging by severity.
g.text: cost high · speed medium · rigor high

g.title: Taste polish: Done and good have split: the artifact works but must match a named, inspectable reference, and the polish can be judged from captures.
g.text: Done and good have split: the artifact works
but must match a named, inspectable…
cost high · speed slow · rigor high

g.title: Tournament then judge: Cheap candidates, then spend the expensive critic on finalists: the approach is open, drafts are cheap, and comparing working options beats arguing about them.
g.text: Cheap candidates, then spend the expensive
critic on finalists: the approach is open…
cost medium · speed fast · rigor standard

g.title: Human-gated irreversible step: A step cannot be undone (merge, spend, publish, delete) and must wait for a human decision; this fragment satisfies E_IRREVERSIBLE_NO_GATE.
g.text: A step cannot be undone (merge, spend,
cost low · speed fast · rigor standard

g.title: Merge queue: Several reviewed changes wait to land together and the integration command (build, lint, tests) is the arbiter: insert this before the host's stop node so a batch lands only green and only on a human's word.
g.text: Several reviewed changes wait to land
cost low · speed medium · rigor standard

g.title: How to read a glyph

svg.text: dashed cell: a fragment, to insert into a graph
One recorded run on a small task shows how a shape behaved once. It does not show that a shape beats the same instructions given as a prompt.
